text:
oncall-bot: Paging: Dedicated-pool alert for customer CobaltHealth (vpc-cobalt-prod). GPU node gpu-7 in pool cohort-3 entered thermal-constraint -> automatic drain started. Severity: P1.

maria.k: saw the page, jumping in. Confirming: this is a Dedicated pool (cohort-3) backing CobaltHealth's VPC, correct? Any live jobs impacted?

sanjay.p: yes, confirmed. cohort-3 is CobaltHealth reserved pool. Node gpu-7 hit 85C sustained, NVLINK errors in dmesg, daemon triggered drain. Some pods flagged for preemptible fallback.

alex.r: quick status: autoscaler kicked, 3 rerouted requests to fallback-model-small, latency spikes ~250-400ms for inflight requests. No API 5xx yet but tail latency increased.

maria.k: @ops-team start tenant isolation check. We need to ensure other CobaltHealth tenants in the same rack are not influenced. If isolation fails -> customer-facing errors.

ops-team: running isolation check now. Running: ```kubectl get pods -n cobalt-prod -o wide | grep cohort-3```

ops-team: output shows 4 pods were on gpu-7, they were gracefully evicted. Two restarted on gpu-9 and gpu-11. One moved to dedicated-fallback-01, one failed to rebind and is Pending.

ryan.t: which pod is Pending? can we force a reschedule to a different node? I can manually intervene if scheduling constraints are blocking.

ops-team: pending is cobalt-infer-agg-02, status: "0/10 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu". Looks like quota bump required in that AZ.

maria.k: immediate actions: 1) open emergency capacity request to Dedicated pool admin to unblock scheduling 2) apply temporary per-tenant routing rule to divert CobaltHealth critical routes to standby region 3) start hardware replace workflow for gpu-7.

alex.r: Started step 2: routing change applied at edge for paths /v1/cobalt/* -> standby-cobalt-us-west (80% traffic), fallback small model for non-critical endpoints. Watch for mismatch in model versions.

sanjay.p: on step 3: I put gpu-7 into "quarantine" and raised HV ticket HV-8427 for HW swap (possible fan/VRAM sensor). On-call assigned to hw-run: @ryan.t can you coordinate on-site bench validation?

ryan.t: I can take hw-run. ETA 25m to validate and attempt one safe reboot if sensor allows. If still failing we'll schedule replacement.

deploy-bot: Canary roll started for routing change (canary 1/5 at 10% -> passed). No errors in endpoint test harness.

maria.k: customer comms draft: "CobaltHealth: We're investigating a dedicated GPU node degradation in your reserved pool. We've isolated affected tenants and routed critical traffic to standby. Expect degraded latency for a subset of requests while we replace hardware. Updates every 30 minutes." Agree?

sanjay.p: looks good. Add note: "no data exfiltration, inference results may be delayed".

maria.k: updated and sent to AE. AE confirmed they'll relay to customer.

ops-team: quick mitigation: bumped dedicated pool quota for cohort-3 in us-west-2 from 12->14 (temporary) which freed scheduling for pending pod. cobalt-infer-agg-02 now running on gpu-11.

alex.r: latency now falling to baseline for most routes; tail still at ~180ms for some heavy contexts. Observability: token-level cost spike on fallback-model-small noted.

maria.k: action items assigned: 
- ryan.t: hw validation + replace plan (HV-8427)
- sanjay.p: follow up on NVLINK logs and open-runbook notes for thermal threshold tuning
- alex.r: verify model parity on fallback and run golden prompt checks
- ops-team: revert quota bump after stabilization and document in incident log

ryan.t: boot logs after soft reboot attached: ```[  112.345] GPU7 fan RPM fluctuating 0->4600 -> sensor timeout -> forced drain``` I'm moving to hardware bench. If we confirm sensor fault we will hot-swap GPU board.

ops-team: we also saw a spot-interruption signal earlier in the region from provider for a different host in cohort-3, but it didn't affect CobaltHealth reserved instances — logging as noise. Marking as monitored.

maria.k: note for postmortem: 1) reduce single-node tenant density for reserved pools (we had 4 pods on gpu-7) 2) add early preflight for quota checks during drain to avoid pending pods 3) ensure fallback model matches major version to avoid quality regressions.

sanjay.p: putting temporary runbook snippet in eng-runtime knowledge base: "If nvlink/aer in dmesg during drain -> quarantine node, soft-reboot once, if persists -> schedule board replacement and re-run kernel diagnostics."

alex.r: will run golden prompt eval after replacement and post results here. If >2% quality delta -> automatic rollback of routing to original model and customer notified.

deploy-bot: Canary finished (5/5) - routing change promoted. No new errors detected in smoke tests.

maria.k: updating incident status: mitigated -> degraded-service. Hardware replace in progress. Next update in 30m or on hw swap completion.

ryan.t: hardware bench confirms fan sensor dead, ordering replacement board, ETA 6 hours for field swap. We can keep node quarantined.

ops-team: after quota adjustment and routing, CobaltHealth reports no user-facing failures. AE will keep customer informed.

maria.k: closing loop: will open full incident postmortem ticket and link HV-8427 + runbook diffs. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident thread archived to incidents-log with id IN-2432105555.
